rows.b: A low-power computer built around a paper-like display that holds thousands of books. It reads for weeks on one charge.
A small device that runs AI right where it sits — a camera that counts cars, a speaker that hears commands — with no internet needed. Private and instant.
A mercury-delay-line memory machine that ran real scientific jobs for university researchers, including programs for biology and radio astronomy. Users prepared programs on punched tape.

Seventeen thousand vacuum tubes performed additions at electronic speed, programmed by plugging cables into panels like a telephone switchboard. A calculation that took days by hand finished in seconds.
